title: Repertoire of the Minneapolis dance band: waltzes, Charleston, Tiger Rag
summary: The Young dance band played waltzes and popular tunes such as Bye Bye Blackbird, Melancholy Baby and The Stampede, with plenty of solo room.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: But let's not get into that. Anyway, we were talking about Lester getting into the tenor, but let's get back a little bit more... We were talking about the records that he was listening to. I think the last thing we were talking about in terms of the chronological story is that you said you were in Minneapolis in 1927, and you were playing with a dance band that Mr. Young had formed.
Yeah.

Now, you have already told about the carnival show, the vaudeville show, the minstrel show, and now you're starting to talk about... Well, then you talked about that show that Mrs. Young had, and then you started to talk about the dance band.
Yeah.

You've already told us about the records you were listening to. At this point, can you tell us something about the kinds of music that were actually played by that dance band that was formed up in Minneapolis?
Oh, they was playing the regular kind of music. Waltzes. People waltzed in them days. We played waltzes. We played tunes like...
Phillips - 71
Well, you were doing waltzes before, right?

Well, we wasn't playin' no dances. Like, if you played a waltz, somebody's gonna dance a waltz or something like that. But I'm talking about in a band, you had to play a waltz if you played a dance, or people would think you was crazy. Because a lot of people liked to waltz, you know. The waltz was kind of a popular thing in them days. And you played tunes like "The Charleston" -- people were doing the Charleston then. And you played "I Want A Little Girl," all them tunes -- of course, they play them now. I heard Buck Clayton playing it the other night, "I Want A Little Girl." And they were playing "If I Could Be With You."
A James P. Johnson tune.
Yeah, he wrote that. He died, didn't he.
Yeah, he died back in the 50's.
I'm trying to think of some of the tunes we played... "Back up all my carin'..." -- "Bye, Bye Blackbird."
This was in the Young dance band.
Yeah. And those were the kinds of tunes that we were playing. We was playing, like, "Fivé foot two, eyes of blue..." Let's see... "My Blue Helper." "Melancholy Baby."
Well, anyway...
Wait a minute. I was getting one. I was trying to think. I was going back, trying to get these...
Phillips - 72
It's a long ways back to think, you know.
[PAUSE]
What was that other tune?
"I'm Coming, Virginia." We said "Stampede."
Off the Fletcher Henderson record.
Yeah, we used to play that. "Tiger Rag."
Was Lester getting solos on this? Was Mr. Young giving you guys a chance to improvise solos?
Oh, man, yeah. You could play all the solos you want. Les was blowin', tearing that alto up. And I was blowing that trumpet. We had another cat in there played good trumpet. He had two trombones.
